central_scientific_result: The public below-5% Seebeck method ceiling does not identify the sign or order of magnitude of the nominal 3.067 mW common-mode response. Two smooth, monotone, alpha-preserving equal-additive drift cases inside that ceiling give opposite-signed reoptimized port responses. The result must therefore remain a nominal scenario until paired raw Seebeck slopes and their calibration/covariance records are obtained.

figure_metadata.core_conclusion: Smooth alpha-preserving Seebeck candidates inside the published method ceiling produce opposite port-effect signs; 3.07 mW is not identified.
evidence_chain: M(T) pointwise ceiling and smooth alpha-preserving cases
Gamma(T) under interpolation and common temperature drift
figure_metadata.layout: quantitative grid with an emphasized identifiability envelope
figure_metadata.limitation: public data lack raw repeats and covariance; the monotone corner screen is complete over binary locally active corners but not a certified global extremum over all continuous error functions
figure_metadata.statistics: deterministic admissible cases and finite-difference sensitivities; no confidence interval, p-value, probability, or inferred covariance

raw_data_priorities.reason: The four largest local response sensitivities are the p/n 323- and 373-K knots; opposite sensitivity signs make their covariance decisive.
raw_data_priorities.request: Paired same-run raw p- and n-leg Seebeck voltage/DeltaT records and replicates at 323 and 373 K, including their cross-leg covariance

raw_data_priorities.reason: An equal additive drift preserves alpha but changes Gamma and is already sufficient to reverse the modeled port-effect sign within the method ceiling.
raw_data_priorities.request: ZEM-3 reference-material, thermocouple, polarity-reversal, and temperature-dependent calibration-drift records for each run

raw_data_priorities.reason: The target temperature field lies entirely in this interval; later knots do not influence the PCHIP response.
raw_data_priorities.request: Dense numeric S_p(T), S_n(T) tables over 300--375 K with specimen IDs, repeat counts, temperature errors, and covariance rather than plotted markers

raw_data_priorities.reason: Without sample identity the best possible curve-level calibration still does not validate the material-specific device attribution.
raw_data_priorities.request: A traceable mapping between the measured transport specimens and the actual p/n legs used in the seven-pair device
